Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. A few items came up from our legal team as they review the DPA redlines:

- Primary retention: they want confirmation that primary production data for our enterprise account will be retained only for the active contract term + 1 year, unless otherwise requested.
- Backups & snapshots: they want tighter language around backups. Specifically: can Redwood commit that backups will be retained no longer than 90 days after deletion in production? They also want a guarantee of onshore processing where we selected the US region.
- Certified deletion: when we request deletion of a customer dataset we need a certified deletion statement (signed) that covers primary + backups + any onshore copies. Is that something Redwood can provide as part of the DPA?
- Evidence: SOC 2 supplement and a sample deletion certificate would help speed procurement.

I've attached our annotated redlines (we'll send a marked-up copy if useful). We're aiming to complete legal review by end of next week.

Appreciate your help — Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi & Marissa to cover the technical and legal bits; below is a proposed compromise we can bake into the DPA redline:

- Primary retention: Redwood will retain production data for the active contract term + 12 months by default. Customer may request earlier deletion via the Support/Console workflow.
- Backups and snapshots: to balance restore risk and data minimization we propose an explicit backup retention cap of 120 days from the date of deletion in production (not 90). Backups are immutable snapshots used for disaster recovery and are only accessible to engineering on a need-to-restore basis.
- Onshore processing / geofencing: for accounts claiming US residency we will ensure processing and backups are in approved US regions unless otherwise agreed in writing; cross-border access will be logged and subject to geo-fallback rules.
- Certified deletion: Redwood will provide a deletion attestation that includes: timestamped job id, list of affected logical identifiers, KMS key destruction metadata (where applicable), and a signed statement from Redwood Security.

Attached is an updated redline that captures the language above and a high-level deletion workflow. Rishi — could you add a short technical note about how backups are purged and what we can include in the attestation? Marissa — please review the suggested phrasing for 'certified deletion' and let me know what legal changes you want.

Emily, is Datavoice comfortable with 120 days for backups? If not, tell us why 90 is a hard requirement and we'll try to bridge it.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical note to support Monica's proposed language and to explain what we can realistically attest to:

1) Backup lifecycle: our backup system takes daily snapshots and retains them for a maximum of 120 days after the object is deleted in prod. Snapshots are stored encrypted with customer-unique prefixes and access is strictly controlled. We can declare in the DPA that backups older than 120 days are scheduled for secure purge and will not be restored except under an explicit, logged restore request.

2) Certified deletion process: when a deletion request is accepted we do a three-step process: (a) logical tombstone in primary store (fast), (b) a background job that deletes KV/objects and rotates KMS keys for the customer namespace, (c) mark related backups for purge at the next snapshot lifecycle job. For the attestation we can provide: the job IDs, KMS rotation event IDs, purge timestamps, and a summary hash of removed object IDs.

3) Onshore copies: for US-resident accounts we pin resources to specific regions and maintain a documented list of physical regions for audit. Any cross-region replication is explicitly disabled unless requested.

4) Proof deliverables: we can deliver a signed deletion certificate PDF and an exportable log snippet (redacted) that shows the KMS events. We cannot provide raw backup contents; we can provide cryptographic evidence (hashes + timestamps) and KMS operation records.

I've attached a short deletion_playbook that we use internally; it can be referenced in the DPA as an internal procedure.

Happy to join a short call to walk through these steps.

— Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: deletion_playbook.txt (text)

Emily — thanks for the patience. I reviewed Monica and Rishi's proposals and suggest the following legal edits to be inserted into the DPA:

- Definition: 'Certified Deletion' shall mean the completion of our deletion workflow that includes logical deletion, KMS key rotation (if applicable), and backup purge scheduling. It shall be accompanied by a signed deletion certificate containing job identifiers and timestamps.
- Backup window: we are prepared to agree to 120 days for backups (instead of 90) but will add explicit language that backups are immutable snapshots used solely for disaster recovery and that Redwood will not restore backups to serve continued processing without Customer approval.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a Sample Deletion Certificate and a SOC 2 Type II supplement specific to data disposal controls within 5 business days of countersignature.
- Legal hold & exceptions: Customer legal holds will pause the scheduled purge for the affected data; Redwood will expose a documented legal-hold request form and logging.

If this aligns with Datavoice's compliance needs we'll update the DPA to DPA_Redline_v3 and circulate for countersignature. DocuSign prepared link below for an expedited path if that helps.

Next steps: Monica, confirm whether we should shorten the backup cap to 90 based on Emily's reply, otherwise we'll move forward with 120-day language and include the sample deletion cert.
